en: The Sūtra on the True Matter Spoken by the Buddha for the Young Bhikṣus, translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmakṣema of the Western Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
During the summer retreat (*varṣā*), many senior *śrāvaka* elders were observing the retreat under trees and in caves near the World-Honored One.

At that time, a great number of junior bhikṣus went to where the Buddha was, prostrated at his feet, and withdrew to sit to one side. For those junior bhikṣus, the Buddha preached the Dharma in various ways, instructing, exhorting, inspiring, and gladdening them.
Having instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened them, he remained silent.
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, those young bhikṣus rejoiced and were filled with joy; they rose from their seats, paid homage, and departed.
The young bhikṣus went to where the elder bhikṣus were, prostrated at the feet of the elders, and sat down to one side.
At that time, the elder bhikṣus thought to themselves:
"We should take these young bhikṣus under our care; let one person accept one person, or let one person accept two, three, or many."
Having formed this thought, he immediately accepted them; he might accept one person for another, or accept two, three, or many people, or even as many as sixty people, including the elders.
At that time, on the fifteenth day of the observance (poṣadha), the World-Honored One arranged his seat before the great assembly and sat down.
Having surveyed the bhikṣus, the World-Honored One addressed them:
“Excellent, excellent!
"I am now pleased that the bhikṣus are performing their various righteous duties; therefore, bhikṣus, you should be diligent and energetic.

At this time, when the month of Kārttika had ended in Śrāvastī, the bhikṣus dwelling in various places throughout the human world heard that the World-Honored One, having completed his rains retreat in Śrāvastī during the month of Kārttika and finished making his robes, was taking up his robe and bowl to travel through the human world from Śrāvastī.

Gradually arriving at Śrāvastī, he took up his robe and bowl, washed his feet, and approached the World-Honored One. Having prostrated himself at the Buddha’s feet in salutation, he withdrew to sit at one side.
At that time, the World-Honored One taught the Dharma in various ways to the bhikṣus of Jambudvīpa.
Having instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened them, he remained silent.
Then, having heard the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma, the bhikṣus of Jambudvīpa rejoiced and were filled with joy; they rose from their seats, paid homage, and departed.
He went to where the elder bhikṣus were, prostrated at their feet, and withdrew to sit at one side.
At that time, the elder bhikṣus thought to themselves:
"We should accept this human bhikṣu; perhaps one person shall accept one person, or two, three, or even many people may accept him. Thereupon, they accepted him.
Some received from one person, some from two, three, or even as many as sixty.
Those elder bhikṣus, having received the bhikṣus from among the people, instructed and exhorted them, being well-versed in the proper sequence of priority.
At that time, on the fifteenth day of the month during the poṣadha ceremony, the World-Honored One arranged his seat before the great assembly and sat down.
Surveying the bhikṣus, he addressed them:
“Excellent, excellent!
"Monks, I rejoice in the righteous conduct you practice; I delight in the righteous conduct that accords with the Dharma.
Monks, the Buddhas of the past also had assemblies of monks whose righteous conduct was just like that of this assembly here."
The assemblies of all future Buddhas shall likewise be thus; their practice of the right path shall be just like that of this present assembly. Why is this?

Within this present assembly, there are elder bhikṣus who have attained the first dhyāna, the second dhyāna, the third dhyāna, and the fourth dhyāna; who have attained loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity; and who have fully dwelt in the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

There is a bhikṣu who, having exhausted the three fetters, attains the stage of Srotāpanna; he does not fall into the evil destinies, is fixed in the Dharma toward full enlightenment (samyak-saṃbodhi), and after seven more births among gods and humans, reaches the ultimate end of suffering.
There is a bhikṣu who, having exhausted the three fetters, has attenuated lust, hatred, and delusion, and attains the stage of Sakṛdāgāmin.
There is a bhikṣu who, having exhausted the five lower fetters, attains the stage of Anāgāmin; he attains parinirvāṇa upon rebirth and shall no longer return to this world.

There are bhikṣus who have attained the immeasurable spheres of supernormal powers: the divine ear, knowledge of the minds of others, knowledge of past lives, knowledge of the death and rebirth of beings, and knowledge of the exhaustion of outflows;

there are bhikṣus who cultivate the contemplation of impurity to sever greed, cultivate loving-kindness to sever ill-will, cultivate the perception of impermanence to sever the conceit "I am," and cultivate mindfulness of breathing to sever discursive thoughts.
How does a bhikṣu cultivate mindfulness of breathing (ānāpānasmṛti) to eliminate perceptions of ideation?

This bhikṣu, depending on a village, up to the point of observing the exhalation that ceases—just as one observes the perception of the exhalation that ceases—is said to be cultivating mindfulness of breathing to eliminate perceptions of ideation.
When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the bhikṣus, having heard what the Buddha taught, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
This concludes the Sutra on the True Matter Spoken by the Buddha for the Young Bhikṣus.
